original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Exact complete single-ADD coefficient repair localization on rational scalar programs, with one source-bound P104 demonstration.
scope_change_reason: PR5568 explicitly asks for event localization beyond the toolkit's endpoint-only fault report. This is a diagnostic capability extension, not a replay speed comparison or a predecessor audit.
bottleneck_link: A complete semantic repair set identifies which event to inspect without replacing the owning native/caller verifier. This is supporting verification tooling, not a new recursive construction.
stop_rule: Stop at the first working exact P104 localization; package the proof and controls without extending to other fault models.
evidence: PROOF.md gives a necessary-and-sufficient repair identity; verify.py compares exact complete repair sets with independent full-program scalar-basis replays and demonstrates the unique repair of one P104 coefficient fault.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which P104 coefficient sites have indistinguishable complete repair signatures?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Endpoint observations can identify only an equivalence class when several events admit the same repair.
open_questions.first_step: Freeze one word and compare normalized nonzero prefix/suffix signatures, including overwritten or zero-source sites.
open_questions.blocked_by: No complete P104 fault-class census is claimed here.

open_questions.question: Can a localized semantic repair be joined to the owning legality checker?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A scalar endpoint repair alone does not certify native frames, ownership or legal erasure.
open_questions.first_step: Pass the reported event and coefficient to an explicit copy of the owning verifier and retain its complete obligations.
open_questions.blocked_by: The current tool deliberately returns suggestions and does not modify words or admit suppliers.

claim_type: scoped diagnostic proof with finite evidence
